pins.name: Corban University
pins.description:
Cascade Collegiate Conference

Visit

Corban University Athletics is committed to fielding teams of Christian student athletes who represent Christ and the University at a top level of competition. Athletics at Corban exists to integrate and enhance the mission of the University, while providing student-athletes and the college community opportunities for spiritual, academic, and athletic growth and development.

We understand, from the Christian perspective, that competition is healthy for growing maturing Christians student-athletes. Studentathletes who are fortunate enough to be a Warrior are provided and challenged with enriched, quality, and competitive intercollegiate athletic opportunities at a national level.

Personal growth is highly emphasized and enhanced by combining spiritual truth into athletic and academic achievement. Coaches actively recruit student-athletes who are committed to developing Christlike character through discipline, teamwork, competition, and ministry. It is a primary goal that all our young men and women display that character and attitude toward opponents, spectators, officials and the community.

Student-athletes at Corban can expect to be challenged, instructed, encouraged and mentored in the process of growing and living life in the image of Jesus Christ. As a member of the Cascade Collegiate Conference (CCC), Corban is affiliated with the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA). Warrior teams compete in women's basketball, cross country, track & field, golf, soccer, softball, lacrosse, volleyball and beach volleyball along with the men's sports of basketball, baseball, cross country, track & field, golf, wrestling and soccer.

Corban has claimed 43 CCC Championships (23 regular-season championships; 20 tournament championships) since all Warrior sports joined the CCC in 1994. Since joining the NAIA prior to the 1970-71 year, Corban University has competed in 44 regional tournament and 83 national tournaments.

In 2022, the Corban beach volleyball team claimed the inaugural NAIA Beach Volleyball National Invitational, Robert Swoboda won the individual national title in the NAIA Track & Field 10,000-meter race, and Valerie Schmidt was crowned the NAIA National Champion in the heptathlon.

The 2022-23 school year featured a pair of NAIA National Tournament Runner-Up team titles for the women's volleyball and beach volleyball programs, where the NAIA National Attacker of the Year (Rylee Troutman) and NAIA Most Valuable Player (Avari Ridgway) paved the way for the two powerhouse rosters.

On an individual basis, Corban men's wrestling standout student-athlete David Rubio set the new standard for the young program, securing his second consecutive CCC Championship at the 165-weight class and finishing as the National Runner-Up at the NAIA National Tournament, the highest individual finish in program history.

Eastern Oregon University, nestled in the picturesque landscapes of La Grande, Oregon, offers a vibrant academic and athletic experience.

Renowned for its commitment to student success and community engagement, EOU provides a supportive environment for students to thrive academically, professionally, and athletically.

At EOU, students can pursue a wide range of academic disciplines, guided by dedicated faculty who prioritize hands-on learning and individualized attention.

The university's emphasis on experiential education equips students with practical skills and knowledge to excel in their chosen fields.

In addition to its academic excellence, EOU boasts a robust athletic program that competes in the Cascade Collegiate Conference and in the Frontier Conference (Football) of the NAIA.

In total Eastern Oregon offers 15 different sports between men’s and women’s programs.

With stateof- the-art facilities and passionate coaching staff, EOU's athletic programs provide student-athletes with opportunities to compete at the highest levels while fostering leadership, discipline, and sportsmanship.

Whether students are pursuing academic endeavors or athletic ambitions, Eastern Oregon University offers a supportive and enriching community where individuals can realize their full potential and create lasting memories.

transcripts.transcript:
I would say the feel of grace is definitely like being at home.

It's so beautiful, and there's tons of green space and the lake, and you just have all this nature around us.

It wasn't just about learning the content.

It wasn't just about a specific degree.

Was about who I was as a person.

It was about who I was as a believer.

It was about who I am as an employee and as a part of the community.

I feel like most of the professors on campus give, give and give and give and give because they believe that their students are here for a reason, for a purpose, that their calling is so much bigger than just a job.

There's just something about being here at school where you'll just walk in and everyone's like, so welcoming to you.

It's just such a different environment than I'm used to.

You walk outside and 50 students are just spread out throughout the campus on the lawns, just doing homework, playing games, whether it's like spike ball or Frisbee.

There's just so many places for students just to go and hang out.

Having this small campus with all these beautiful places and open areas just makes it really easy to feel like you're kind of home, or that feel like you're part of the community right away.

Well, I really like to know my students.

I like to get to know them.

I like to get to understand them, how they're how they're wired.

How can I connect with them in the classroom so that I can foster their learning, so that they can become the professional they need to be.

They learn all this stuff.

They have these aha moments.

They run out, they come back, the next day, you'll have no idea what I did.

I was watching somebody, and then I helped them, and it was so rewarding.

And I'm like, Yes, that's what you're supposed to do.

It empowers them.

I want them to be what they want to be.

And I'm like, How do I get them to do that?

That's like, my greatest challenge as a professor.

Really didn't have plans for college, and at the advice of my father, he said, Well, you know what, just apply for one school.

So my education at Grace, both in the undergraduate and the MBA, have set the stage for me to continue to develop myself and my my knowledge regarding this field.

One of the things that always impressed me about Grace College was they weren't just located in Winona lake.

They were really integrated into those communities.

They were a part of what was happening there.

They were reaching out to some of the organizations and some of the just the neighborhoods that they existed in.

There are a lot of quality people here trying to better our world, that mentality is what we're pushing on to our students, like a lot of classes, faith is just integrated into it.

They want to talk about everything from at least a faith aspect.

That foundation that I set at Grace has has helped me to be a better father, has helped me to be a better employee, has helped me to be a better husband.

That's probably almost more valuable than the education, and that's something that I don't think you probably would get at every college.

transcripts.transcript:
Hello and welcome to this video tour of Bellevue University's main campus.

We're happy to have you with us to show you our beautiful, 46 acre campus in Bellevue Nebraska.

We'll start our journey at the Marge H Durham Student Center, built in 1986 the Student Center serves as a student hub for dining services.

Has patio space for bonfires and hanging out, recreation space for campus events and even a game room.

Less than a block from main campus is the new student housing Betts road complex, open in the fall of 2017 The complex has 18 units with 72 single rooms.

Each apartment has four single bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, a living area and furnishings, including a washer and dryer in each unit.

Next up is the Gordon loggier Athletic Center.

The Athletic Center houses the Jerry mosser court administrative offices and the new eSports arena deemed the Bruin bunker.

The facility is home to the university's NAIA sanctioned sports programs, baseball, softball, volleyball, men's and women's basketball, men's and women's golf, men's and women's soccer and men's and women's cross country.

The CO Ed esports team competes in League of Legends Overwatch and Hearthstone.

What would a college campus be without a library?

The Freeman logger library has the largest library collection in Sarpy County, along with plenty of books, the library includes an integrated media center, which allows students access to computerized and web based resources with training facilities to teach students how to effectively use these resources.

Located in the back hall of the library, the Learning Commons is an important support office with consultants and peer tutors ready to assist you in the tutor and study skills program and writing center.

North of the Learning Center is the newest building on campus, built in 2021 the sustainability lab is complete with a greenhouse, algae pond and more.

Our next stop is the Educational Services Building.

The Educational Services Building, ESB, as is known, houses, classrooms and the College of Science and Technology on its lower level.

On the middle and upper levels, there are additional College of Arts and Science faculty and staff offices, Career Services is also found on the third floor.

Everyone's favorite thing about this building seems to be the amazing indoor waterfall.

Attached to the ESB is the John B Muller Administrative Services Building, or ASB, built in 2011 the ASB is the tallest building in Bellevue Nebraska.

Right inside the front doors is the One Stop Welcome Center and support desk.

One Stop provides a one stop shop for current and prospective students to meet with admissions advising and financial services, staff disability services, as well as scholarships and grants.

Are other helpful resources located in the ASB the Bruin training and athletic center is a regular stop for Bruin student athletes, and has wellness equipment and a weight room that are free for all students to use.

We hope you enjoyed this tour of Bell University's main campus.

See you soon.

Adapting educational technology and teaching methods has ensured all students receive a high-impact learning experience no matter their location or ability.

transcripts.transcript:
What defines you? If you want better results, you must ask better questions.

The right questions awaken incredible power, opening the mind to possibilities and banishing the word impossible.

La Sierra University is defined by the questions it asks.

How can we seek truth and enlarge human understanding through scholarship?

How can we know God ourselves and the world?

How can we serve others and contribute to the good of our local and global communities?

La Sierra University relentlessly asked these fundamental, yet all encompassing questions, the answers have led us to excellence.

We started in a field in 1922 the dust blew so thick that students shoveled it from their dorm rooms, but the founders clung to their vision of values based higher education.

Now la Sierra is a thriving campus of Riverside the city of arts and innovation. We offer more than degrees.

We teach students to be fully alive, to take radical ownership of their faith, their career, their community, their country and their world.

Students dig in one of the longest running excavations in Jordan and study abroad and serve as missionaries in dozens of countries.

They perform in prestigious competitions and venues around the world.

They represent the United States on world stages as the undergraduates.

They co author research in leading publications.

They are athletes who learn that teamwork, discipline and perseverance are the keys to success in all of life's endeavors.

All this defines who we are at La Sierra University, I ask again, what defines you?

transcripts.transcript:
College athletics.

It is the proving ground for elite high school athletes who wish to measure their skill, willpower and fortitude against others who also excel in their craft.

It is not an arena made for the undisciplined or unmotivated.

It rewards those who push their bodies to the limit and punishes the excuse makers for the focused competitors.

The choice of institution will play a pivotal role in how they transition from the glories of high school to the potential of what they can achieve.

St Ambrose is a university where student athletes, serious about academics and being the best they can be in competition, can thrive to their absolute potential.

What distinguishes athletics at St Ambrose as members of our athletic family fighting bee athletes play and practice in facilities which are among the finest to be found in the NAIA.

The Ambrose dome is an indoor facility with batting cages and a golf simulator where outdoor sports can train in winter months and in foul weather.

The Wellness and Recreation Center has a weight room dedicated to athletic teams, as well as an additional weight room and cardio room for all students.

It features a dance studio where competitive dance and cheer can practice routines.

The field house features an indoor track facility with long jump, pole vault, high jump and throwing cages, two wood courts and two courts with multi use surface allow practice space for every sport, including tennis.

Lee Lowman arena hosts basketball, wrestling, volleyball and Winter Guard.

And last year, was the site of the NAIA national cheer and dance competition. Modern Woodman Park is not only home to the Kansas City Royals minor league team, Quad City river bandits, but also hosts the fighting bee baseball program.

St Vincent Sports Complex has a dedicated softball field, as well as three turfed fields that host lacrosse and soccer games, and has practice facilities for football and marching band.

Cumberland University Athletic Department
Statement of Mission, Philosophy and Objective

Mission

The purpose of the intercollegiate athletic program at Cumberland University is to instill in every student-athlete the highest standards of personal integrity and responsibility.

Philosophy

The Cumberland University intercollegiate athletic program provides the opportunity for each student-athlete to develop self-discipline through the setting and achievement of goals in the classroom and in their respective sport.

Objectives

The Cumberland University intercollegiate athletic program is dedicated to:

  • Providing equal opportunity for intercollegiate participation for male and female student-athletes, and all minorities.
  • Supporting the satisfactory academic progress of each student-athlete.
  • Offering intercollegiate programs for both male and female student-athletes.
  • Appropriately representing CU by maintaining sportsmanship and by displaying fair play in competition.
  • Holding student-athletes accountable to standards at or about University’s Regulations on personal behavior.
  • Complying with the policies of the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) and Mid-South Conference.
  • Providing equal access to financial assistance for all qualified student-athletes.
  • Ensuring the physical, emotional and social welfare of each student-athlete.

transcripts.transcript:
Welcome to our woods.

One woods, one woods, 111111 woods. We celebrate our many cultures at one table, bon appetit.

We represent a rainbow of colorful flags, but we are united under one True Blue Flag, from one note to many notes, we create a better sound.

Together with our common language of science, we solve interesting problems from different perspectives and get better results.

We have a shared love of horses and the woods, and we have a shared love of the values that the woods holds.

Growing up in a small town, there wasn't a ton of diversity here at the woods, we've been able to create safe conversations about diversity.

This place has become home, and I don't imagine myself being anywhere else.

I this year, we celebrate and renew our commitment to one woods, one woods, yet no.

OCU is consistently ranked as one of the top universities in the country by U.S. News & World Report and is listed in Forbes' "100 Best College Buys."

At Oklahoma City University, we’re proud to lay claim to the title “Home of Champions.”

Winning championships is what we’re all about, with 73 national titles to our name and a streak of winning at least one national championship each year for the past 30 years.

We give our students something to cheer about, whether you’re taking in a basketball game at the Freede Center, watching a baseball game at Jim Wade Stadium, or supporting any one of our more than 20 varsity teams.

From rowing to wrestling and soccer to softball, OCU student-athletes compete to win and work hard to unite our campus to rally behind the Stars!

Visit the OCU Athletics home page to learn more about our teams and catch up on the latest news.

Wayland Baptist University was founded in 1908 by Dr. James Henry Wayland. Wayland is the oldest institution of higher education in continuous existence on the High Plains of Texas. Wayland Baptist has approximately 1,100 students enrolled at its Plainview campus.

Wayland's home campus is in Plainview, Texas, but Wayland has nine other operating campuses in Lubbock, Amarillo, Wichita Falls and San Antonio, Texas; Phoenix and Sierra Vista, Ariz.; Anchorage and Fairbanks, Alaska; and Mililani, Hawaii. Wayland also offers full degree programs online.

transcripts.transcript:
Hey guys, I'm Josh, and we're in the Hutcherson center, and this is where our women's volleyball team plays, and our men's and women's basketball team, if you look around, you can tell it's a brand new court and a very nice facility.

You'll see our national championship banners, all the red banners that you see, all of those belong to men's or women's, indoor or outdoor track and field, except for one, and that belongs to men's soccer.

Our men's soccer team went down to Florida in 2017 ranked 23rd in the nation.

Had to have a play in game to get into the championship and won the semifinal and quarterfinal games on penalty kicks, and finally, the championship game on a golden goal opportunity.

So a fantastic story, but our track and field program is our most successful program as far as national championships go, every single year between the really four distinctive sports, men and women's, indoor and outdoor track and field, they have an opportunity to win a national championship.

Behind me, you can see some of our flying Queens banners.

That's our women's basketball team, the AAU championship banners that they have.

We're actually going to go into their locker room and talk a little more about their history.

All right, guys.

Now we're in the flying Queens locker room, which is one of our premier locker rooms that we have here at Wayland Baptist University.

This one, for sure, did not come without a lot of hard work and history. Our women's basketball program is the winningest collegiate basketball program in all of the United States.

We're talking UConn women, Tennessee women, UCLA men, Duke men, anybody you can think of, Wayland, Babbage University.

Flying Queens has more wins than any of them. And that flying Queens name, I know, might sound a little strange to you, but it has a really neat story behind it.

The girls were beating everybody in this area, and so a local aviator, Mr. Hutcherson, said, Hey, let's take these girls and try to find some competitions.

They started flying all over the country playing basketball games and in the early 50s and 60s and stuff, they were they had the longest win streak in collegiate basketball history as well, 131 games in a row.

That record still stands today. So the program itself was nominated for the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame several times, and before they got in, they were losing to the names of like Shaquille, O'Neal, Allen, Iverson, Tom Izzo, Yao Ming, Tracy, McGrady, Cheryl swoops, just to give you an idea, we're talking about the greatest names in basketball history.

But in 2019 our girls were finally enshrined into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, which is something we're very proud of, and has a ton of awesome, rich history included.

So now let's go check out another piece of the hutch. Alright guys, we're here in the entryway of the Hutchison center, and what you'll see up here is end to end, wall to wall, trophy cases, and this has things like individual awards, like all American status and team awards, national championships and things like that.

But the one thing that I really want to point out is a an overall Wayland competition, and something that we're really proud of is the Learfield Sports directors cup.

This is a competition put on by the NAI, and there's over 300 nai schools in the United States that compete for this, and Whalen consistently finishes in the top 10.

To do this, I mean, you have to have other sports pull their weight as well. We spoke a little bit about women's basketball, men's soccer, track and field, but all of our sports have to be doing a good job, and they do a really good job.

The other sports we have here at Wayland are men's football, women's volleyball, men's women's cross country, men's and women's wrestling, men's basketball, let's see we have the baseball program, the cheer and dance program, men's women's golf, and so all of our programs here compete at a very high level, and it's something that you can be a part of.

I hope that you liked this video.

If you want to check out the other videos on the campus tour playlist, that'd be awesome.

And if you'd like to apply to Wayland, go to wbu.edu and click the Apply button.

Thanks.

Life is unique in that it's a small school with a lot of diversity.

The cool thing about this school is like walking around and just hearing different accents everywhere.

It's not a very big school, but I feel like it's a very authentic school. Majority of the school is athletes.

I feel like everyone understands the struggles and that we're more than just rugby players or soccer players or vulnerable players, that there is other stuff besides that that we need to work with and like get around to make sure that we hit our goals.

You know, being a student in an in and of itself is a difficult thing.

Matching that with being an athlete is a whole nother ball game. Being in DC as well as an RA and a student athlete, that is actually a work in progress. But one thing has helped me from the start of the DC program and being an RA to now is time management.

It's easy to be a student athlete.

If you want to be good in class, you're gonna find time to study.

If you like what you're studying, of course you're gonna spend more time on that.

But it's not, it's not hard work playing both soccer and being in the DC program.

Is extremely hard to like, I'm not gonna lie, I'm late to school because of practice, or I'm late to practice because of school.

And I'm always like running between the two places, which is sad, but at the end of the day, like, I'm so, so grateful that I can do both these things.

Being a discomfort situation leads to an improvement of yourself.

Make you, make your yourself tougher, and helps you, helps you develop and gets better every day.

So for example, from making the bed as soon as you wake up to doing the little things but you gotta do, leads to bigger improvements in the future.

One of the greatest pleasures of being a collegiate athlete is that you get to be a part of a team environment.

You meet people from all around the world with different backgrounds, cultures, religions, perspectives on life, and that's something quite special.

So I think it's a privilege to be a student athlete, because not everybody can tell about themselves that they go to university study and also do their sport and also just, you know, making friends.

I think it's so much fun. I always try to finish everything as soon as possible.

So then I'm I'm free to enjoy my day with my friends or doing new experiences, I feel like, what makes it better as an athlete here is really the trainer, like, obviously for me, having, like, my meniscus torn and being through all the injuries and having to play on it, she's really keeping me going right now, just because I'm training with her consistently, where our coaches definitely set the standard from day one, whether it's from the recruitment process to practice the weights, you know, they make sure we're always on point and, you know, ready for anything.

Not a lot of people get to train every day.

Have all the resources.

Have a coach, have a PT, have people to push you.

I understand that it's an absolute privilege to wear the eagle on a Saturday, and it's something that many people don't get the opportunity to do.

I've learned so many lessons, but I think the most important you need to trust the process.

It has.

It's gonna have so many setbacks, but the way you react on things that's really important.

Time passes by really fast.

Opportunities come at you really fast, and if you let them go, they're gone.

So I just say that do as much as you can and enjoy it as much as you can.

Nestled in the heart of Pulaski, TN, the University of Tennessee Southern is dedicated to putting students first, catering to the diverse needs of our small-town community.

As a destination campus deeply committed to the student experience, we prioritize both academic excellence and the personal growth of every student.

UT Southern proudly stands as the fourth undergraduate campus in the UT System, serving as the sole public four-year institution of higher education between Chattanooga and Memphis.

Conveniently located along Tennessee’s southern border, our campus is situated approximately 70 miles south of Nashville and 40 miles north of Huntsville, Alabama.

Here's what makes us stand out: We offer 38 areas of study across six schools, providing tailored learning experiences with small classes and esteemed professors.

Our academic divisions focus on business, education, humanities, mathematics and sciences, nursing, and social sciences.

With a robust athletics department boasting 19 teams across 11 sports, UT Southern has something for everyone. We prioritize character development through 19 NAIA varsity sports, with an impressive record of 40 Mid-South Conference Championships and 12 National Championships.

Our commitment to success extends beyond the field, with 75 Athletic All-Americans and 215 Academic All-Americans recognized. Offering 11 Men's, 12 Women's, and 2 Coed Sports, we provide a comprehensive athletic experience.

UT Southern is dedicated to evolving our curriculum to reflect industry trends and technological advancements, emphasizing interdisciplinary studies for a well-rounded education.

We empower students to discover their passions, foster critical thinking skills, and graduate prepared for successful careers in an ever-changing world. At UT Southern, excellence is not just a goal—it's our commitment to every student who walks through our doors.

Indiana Tech is a comprehensive university that educates students beyond its home base of Fort Wayne, Indiana, with nine regional service centers and online programs that meet the needs of students worldwide.

This private, not-for-profit university specializes in career-oriented degree and certificate programs in wide variety of disciplines that include business, engineering, computer sciences, criminal justice, cybersecurity, marketing, health sciences, communication and helping professions.

We prepare students for active participation, career advancement, and leadership in the global 21st century society, and motivate them toward lives of significance and worth. Indiana Tech’s Department of Athletics fields 29 collegiate teams.

The university has been recognized as an NAIA Champions of Character Five-Star Institution since the inception of the award in 2002. In 2023, Indiana Tech won the Learfield Directors’ Cup for having the NAIA’s most successful athletic program during the 2022-23 academic year.

Go for it.

Music.

This is a special place.

God is moving on this campus.

You won't just get a degree here you will get a relevant education anchored in the biblical worldview from people who will help you transform your future.

We love the people in our community, and the church is where we serve, and we don't want to stop there. We want to impact and help transform the lives of the people we encounter in our future, in our families, around our neighborhoods, and throughout our careers, we believe that Hannibal Lagrange University is where you belong.

HlG and you you were meant to b e here on this campus, expanding your knowledge through intentional study, making memories with forever friends, having a good laugh, living out life with a purpose, experiencing God as he prepares you for the next chapter in your life, being present in His presence.

What can we say? This place feels like home? HlG feels like home.

It's like home. HlG is home.

HlG, is more than just a campus.

It's a place to be a part of the community.

When you graduate as a Trojan, you leave here changed better than when you first walked onto campus.

You can find God's plan for your future here at HlG this is where I belong, where we belong, where I belong.

This is where you belong.

Our scenic campus provides students with an enriching environment that fosters personal growth and a sense of community. Athletic Program Highlights Bryan College is a proud member of the NAIA, with a robust athletics program that includes 16 varsity sports.

Our teams, known as the Lions, are recognized for their competitive spirit, sportsmanship, and academic achievements.

Our facilities, such as the Summers Gymnasium and the brand-new baseball and softball complexes, offer top-notch environments for training and competition.

Studentathletes who are fortunate enough to be a Warrior are provided and challenged with enriched, quality, and competitive intercollegiate athletic opportunities at a national level.

Personal growth is highly emphasized and enhanced by combining spiritual truth into athletic and academic achievement. Coaches actively recruit student-athletes who are committed to developing Christlike character through discipline, teamwork, competition, and ministry. It is a primary goal that all our young men and women display that character and attitude toward opponents, spectators, officials and the community.

Student-athletes at Corban can expect to be challenged, instructed, encouraged and mentored in the process of growing and living life in the image of Jesus Christ. As a member of the Cascade Collegiate Conference (CCC), Corban is affiliated with the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA). Warrior teams compete in women's basketball, cross country, track & field, golf, soccer, softball, lacrosse, volleyball and beach volleyball along with the men's sports of basketball, baseball, cross country, track & field, golf, wrestling and soccer.

Corban has claimed 43 CCC Championships (23 regular-season championships; 20 tournament championships) since all Warrior sports joined the CCC in 1994. Since joining the NAIA prior to the 1970-71 year, Corban University has competed in 44 regional tournament and 83 national tournaments.

In 2022, the Corban beach volleyball team claimed the inaugural NAIA Beach Volleyball National Invitational, Robert Swoboda won the individual national title in the NAIA Track & Field 10,000-meter race, and Valerie Schmidt was crowned the NAIA National Champion in the heptathlon.

The 2022-23 school year featured a pair of NAIA National Tournament Runner-Up team titles for the women's volleyball and beach volleyball programs, where the NAIA National Attacker of the Year (Rylee Troutman) and NAIA Most Valuable Player (Avari Ridgway) paved the way for the two powerhouse rosters.

On an individual basis, Corban men's wrestling standout student-athlete David Rubio set the new standard for the young program, securing his second consecutive CCC Championship at the 165-weight class and finishing as the National Runner-Up at the NAIA National Tournament, the highest individual finish in program history.

transcripts.transcript:
I would say the feel of grace is definitely like being at home.

It's so beautiful, and there's tons of green space and the lake, and you just have all this nature around us.

It wasn't just about learning the content.

It wasn't just about a specific degree.

Was about who I was as a person.

It was about who I was as a believer.

It was about who I am as an employee and as a part of the community.

I feel like most of the professors on campus give, give and give and give and give because they believe that their students are here for a reason, for a purpose, that their calling is so much bigger than just a job.

There's just something about being here at school where you'll just walk in and everyone's like, so welcoming to you.

It's just such a different environment than I'm used to.

You walk outside and 50 students are just spread out throughout the campus on the lawns, just doing homework, playing games, whether it's like spike ball or Frisbee.

There's just so many places for students just to go and hang out.

Having this small campus with all these beautiful places and open areas just makes it really easy to feel like you're kind of home, or that feel like you're part of the community right away.

Well, I really like to know my students.

I like to get to know them.

I like to get to understand them, how they're how they're wired.

How can I connect with them in the classroom so that I can foster their learning, so that they can become the professional they need to be.

They learn all this stuff.

They have these aha moments.

They run out, they come back, the next day, you'll have no idea what I did.

I was watching somebody, and then I helped them, and it was so rewarding.

And I'm like, Yes, that's what you're supposed to do.

It empowers them.

I want them to be what they want to be.

And I'm like, How do I get them to do that?

That's like, my greatest challenge as a professor.

Really didn't have plans for college, and at the advice of my father, he said, Well, you know what, just apply for one school.

So my education at Grace, both in the undergraduate and the MBA, have set the stage for me to continue to develop myself and my my knowledge regarding this field.

One of the things that always impressed me about Grace College was they weren't just located in Winona lake.

They were really integrated into those communities.

They were a part of what was happening there.

They were reaching out to some of the organizations and some of the just the neighborhoods that they existed in.

There are a lot of quality people here trying to better our world, that mentality is what we're pushing on to our students, like a lot of classes, faith is just integrated into it.

They want to talk about everything from at least a faith aspect.

That foundation that I set at Grace has has helped me to be a better father, has helped me to be a better employee, has helped me to be a better husband.

That's probably almost more valuable than the education, and that's something that I don't think you probably would get at every college.

transcripts.transcript:
Hello and welcome to this video tour of Bellevue University's main campus.

We're happy to have you with us to show you our beautiful, 46 acre campus in Bellevue Nebraska.

We'll start our journey at the Marge H Durham Student Center, built in 1986 the Student Center serves as a student hub for dining services.

Has patio space for bonfires and hanging out, recreation space for campus events and even a game room.

Less than a block from main campus is the new student housing Betts road complex, open in the fall of 2017 The complex has 18 units with 72 single rooms.

Each apartment has four single bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, a living area and furnishings, including a washer and dryer in each unit.

Next up is the Gordon loggier Athletic Center.

The Athletic Center houses the Jerry mosser court administrative offices and the new eSports arena deemed the Bruin bunker.

The facility is home to the university's NAIA sanctioned sports programs, baseball, softball, volleyball, men's and women's basketball, men's and women's golf, men's and women's soccer and men's and women's cross country.

The CO Ed esports team competes in League of Legends Overwatch and Hearthstone.

What would a college campus be without a library?

The Freeman logger library has the largest library collection in Sarpy County, along with plenty of books, the library includes an integrated media center, which allows students access to computerized and web based resources with training facilities to teach students how to effectively use these resources.

Located in the back hall of the library, the Learning Commons is an important support office with consultants and peer tutors ready to assist you in the tutor and study skills program and writing center.

North of the Learning Center is the newest building on campus, built in 2021 the sustainability lab is complete with a greenhouse, algae pond and more.

Our next stop is the Educational Services Building.

The Educational Services Building, ESB, as is known, houses, classrooms and the College of Science and Technology on its lower level.

On the middle and upper levels, there are additional College of Arts and Science faculty and staff offices, Career Services is also found on the third floor.

Everyone's favorite thing about this building seems to be the amazing indoor waterfall.

Attached to the ESB is the John B Muller Administrative Services Building, or ASB, built in 2011 the ASB is the tallest building in Bellevue Nebraska.

Right inside the front doors is the One Stop Welcome Center and support desk.

One Stop provides a one stop shop for current and prospective students to meet with admissions advising and financial services, staff disability services, as well as scholarships and grants.

Are other helpful resources located in the ASB the Bruin training and athletic center is a regular stop for Bruin student athletes, and has wellness equipment and a weight room that are free for all students to use.

We hope you enjoyed this tour of Bell University's main campus.

See you soon.

Recognized as one of the top public regional colleges in the Midwest and one of America’s “Best Colleges” for 26 consecutive years by U.S. News, VCSU is an academically driven, student-centered university.

VCSU offers more than 65 undergraduate programs in art, business, communication arts, computer systems and software engineering, education, kinesiology and human performance, language and literature, mathematics, music, science, social science, and technology education.

VCSU’s athletic department features 15 intercollegiate sports including football, women’s volleyball, men’s and women’s cross country, men’s and women’s basketball, men’s and women’s indoor track & field, baseball, softball, men’s and women’s golf, men’s and women’s outdoor track & field, and coed trap shooting.

Student-athletes make up about 35 percent of our on-campus students.

Valley City State University holds the title for the best elementary education program in the country, outranking non-profit public and private schools.

Founded in 1890 as a teacher’s college, VCSU has held fast to its heritage and maintains an outstanding reputation for developing some of the finest K – 12 educators in the region.

By providing full-time students with their own laptop, VCSU has remained committed to accessible, technology-driven educational opportunities for all students.

Adapting educational technology and teaching methods has ensured all students receive a high-impact learning experience no matter their location or ability.

Located in Valley City, a town of 6,500 people along the Sheyenne River, VCSU’s 55-acre campus is bordered on the south by a forested hillside and on the north by the Sheyenne River.

transcripts.transcript:
What defines you? If you want better results, you must ask better questions.

The right questions awaken incredible power, opening the mind to possibilities and banishing the word impossible.

La Sierra University is defined by the questions it asks.

How can we seek truth and enlarge human understanding through scholarship?

How can we know God ourselves and the world?

How can we serve others and contribute to the good of our local and global communities?

La Sierra University relentlessly asked these fundamental, yet all encompassing questions, the answers have led us to excellence.

We started in a field in 1922 the dust blew so thick that students shoveled it from their dorm rooms, but the founders clung to their vision of values based higher education.

Now la Sierra is a thriving campus of Riverside the city of arts and innovation. We offer more than degrees.

We teach students to be fully alive, to take radical ownership of their faith, their career, their community, their country and their world.

Students dig in one of the longest running excavations in Jordan and study abroad and serve as missionaries in dozens of countries.

They perform in prestigious competitions and venues around the world.

They represent the United States on world stages as the undergraduates.

They co author research in leading publications.

They are athletes who learn that teamwork, discipline and perseverance are the keys to success in all of life's endeavors.

All this defines who we are at La Sierra University, I ask again, what defines you?

transcripts.transcript:
College athletics.

It is the proving ground for elite high school athletes who wish to measure their skill, willpower and fortitude against others who also excel in their craft.

It is not an arena made for the undisciplined or unmotivated.

It rewards those who push their bodies to the limit and punishes the excuse makers for the focused competitors.

The choice of institution will play a pivotal role in how they transition from the glories of high school to the potential of what they can achieve.

St Ambrose is a university where student athletes, serious about academics and being the best they can be in competition, can thrive to their absolute potential.

What distinguishes athletics at St Ambrose as members of our athletic family fighting bee athletes play and practice in facilities which are among the finest to be found in the NAIA.

The Ambrose dome is an indoor facility with batting cages and a golf simulator where outdoor sports can train in winter months and in foul weather.

The Wellness and Recreation Center has a weight room dedicated to athletic teams, as well as an additional weight room and cardio room for all students.

It features a dance studio where competitive dance and cheer can practice routines.

The field house features an indoor track facility with long jump, pole vault, high jump and throwing cages, two wood courts and two courts with multi use surface allow practice space for every sport, including tennis.

Lee Lowman arena hosts basketball, wrestling, volleyball and Winter Guard.

And last year, was the site of the NAIA national cheer and dance competition. Modern Woodman Park is not only home to the Kansas City Royals minor league team, Quad City river bandits, but also hosts the fighting bee baseball program.

St Vincent Sports Complex has a dedicated softball field, as well as three turfed fields that host lacrosse and soccer games, and has practice facilities for football and marching band.

Brady Street stadium is the site for st Ambrose football, providing a vibrant Game Day atmosphere, which includes tailgating, marching band dance performances and cheerleading.

Members of fighting bee Athletics will not only enjoy the finest facilities, but will also discover the st Ambrose difference as they cultivate relationships during their experiences, student athletes at sau develop deep bonds with athletic staff at every level, from assistant coaches, head coaches, five athletic trainers, sports information staff, all the way to the athletic director st Ambrose cares about our athletes having a great experience.

It is when top facilities combine with a relationship driven staff that the student athlete at St Ambrose unlocks their potential, finds the best of what they can become, and experiences the transition from what could be to the summit of achievement.

Cumberland University Athletic Department
Statement of Mission, Philosophy and Objective

Mission

The purpose of the intercollegiate athletic program at Cumberland University is to instill in every student-athlete the highest standards of personal integrity and responsibility.

Philosophy

The Cumberland University intercollegiate athletic program provides the opportunity for each student-athlete to develop self-discipline through the setting and achievement of goals in the classroom and in their respective sport.

Objectives

The Cumberland University intercollegiate athletic program is dedicated to:

  • Providing equal opportunity for intercollegiate participation for male and female student-athletes, and all minorities.
  • Supporting the satisfactory academic progress of each student-athlete.
  • Offering intercollegiate programs for both male and female student-athletes.
  • Appropriately representing CU by maintaining sportsmanship and by displaying fair play in competition.
  • Holding student-athletes accountable to standards at or about University’s Regulations on personal behavior.
  • Complying with the policies of the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) and Mid-South Conference.
  • Providing equal access to financial assistance for all qualified student-athletes.
  • Ensuring the physical, emotional and social welfare of each student-athlete.

Wayland Baptist University was founded in 1908 by Dr. James Henry Wayland. Wayland is the oldest institution of higher education in continuous existence on the High Plains of Texas. Wayland Baptist has approximately 1,100 students enrolled at its Plainview campus.

Wayland's home campus is in Plainview, Texas, but Wayland has nine other operating campuses in Lubbock, Amarillo, Wichita Falls and San Antonio, Texas; Phoenix and Sierra Vista, Ariz.; Anchorage and Fairbanks, Alaska; and Mililani, Hawaii. Wayland also offers full degree programs online.

transcripts.transcript:
Hey guys, I'm Josh, and we're in the Hutcherson center, and this is where our women's volleyball team plays, and our men's and women's basketball team, if you look around, you can tell it's a brand new court and a very nice facility.

You'll see our national championship banners, all the red banners that you see, all of those belong to men's or women's, indoor or outdoor track and field, except for one, and that belongs to men's soccer.

Our men's soccer team went down to Florida in 2017 ranked 23rd in the nation.

Had to have a play in game to get into the championship and won the semifinal and quarterfinal games on penalty kicks, and finally, the championship game on a golden goal opportunity.

So a fantastic story, but our track and field program is our most successful program as far as national championships go, every single year between the really four distinctive sports, men and women's, indoor and outdoor track and field, they have an opportunity to win a national championship.

Behind me, you can see some of our flying Queens banners.

That's our women's basketball team, the AAU championship banners that they have.

We're actually going to go into their locker room and talk a little more about their history.

All right, guys.

Now we're in the flying Queens locker room, which is one of our premier locker rooms that we have here at Wayland Baptist University.

This one, for sure, did not come without a lot of hard work and history. Our women's basketball program is the winningest collegiate basketball program in all of the United States.

We're talking UConn women, Tennessee women, UCLA men, Duke men, anybody you can think of, Wayland, Babbage University.

Flying Queens has more wins than any of them. And that flying Queens name, I know, might sound a little strange to you, but it has a really neat story behind it.

The girls were beating everybody in this area, and so a local aviator, Mr. Hutcherson, said, Hey, let's take these girls and try to find some competitions.

They started flying all over the country playing basketball games and in the early 50s and 60s and stuff, they were they had the longest win streak in collegiate basketball history as well, 131 games in a row.

That record still stands today. So the program itself was nominated for the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame several times, and before they got in, they were losing to the names of like Shaquille, O'Neal, Allen, Iverson, Tom Izzo, Yao Ming, Tracy, McGrady, Cheryl swoops, just to give you an idea, we're talking about the greatest names in basketball history.

But in 2019 our girls were finally enshrined into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, which is something we're very proud of, and has a ton of awesome, rich history included.

So now let's go check out another piece of the hutch. Alright guys, we're here in the entryway of the Hutchison center, and what you'll see up here is end to end, wall to wall, trophy cases, and this has things like individual awards, like all American status and team awards, national championships and things like that.

But the one thing that I really want to point out is a an overall Wayland competition, and something that we're really proud of is the Learfield Sports directors cup.

This is a competition put on by the NAI, and there's over 300 nai schools in the United States that compete for this, and Whalen consistently finishes in the top 10.

To do this, I mean, you have to have other sports pull their weight as well. We spoke a little bit about women's basketball, men's soccer, track and field, but all of our sports have to be doing a good job, and they do a really good job.

The other sports we have here at Wayland are men's football, women's volleyball, men's women's cross country, men's and women's wrestling, men's basketball, let's see we have the baseball program, the cheer and dance program, men's women's golf, and so all of our programs here compete at a very high level, and it's something that you can be a part of.

I hope that you liked this video.

If you want to check out the other videos on the campus tour playlist, that'd be awesome.

And if you'd like to apply to Wayland, go to wbu.edu and click the Apply button.

Thanks.

The cool thing about this school is like walking around and just hearing different accents everywhere.

I feel like everyone understands the struggles and that we're more than just rugby players or soccer players or vulnerable players, that there is other stuff besides that that we need to work with and like get around to make sure that we hit our goals.

You know, being a student in an in and of itself is a difficult thing.

Matching that with being an athlete is a whole nother ball game. Being in DC as well as an RA and a student athlete, that is actually a work in progress. But one thing has helped me from the start of the DC program and being an RA to now is time management.

It's easy to be a student athlete.

If you want to be good in class, you're gonna find time to study.

If you like what you're studying, of course you're gonna spend more time on that.

But it's not, it's not hard work playing both soccer and being in the DC program.

Is extremely hard to like, I'm not gonna lie, I'm late to school because of practice, or I'm late to practice because of school.

And I'm always like running between the two places, which is sad, but at the end of the day, like, I'm so, so grateful that I can do both these things.

Being a discomfort situation leads to an improvement of yourself.

Make you, make your yourself tougher, and helps you, helps you develop and gets better every day.

So for example, from making the bed as soon as you wake up to doing the little things but you gotta do, leads to bigger improvements in the future.

One of the greatest pleasures of being a collegiate athlete is that you get to be a part of a team environment.

You meet people from all around the world with different backgrounds, cultures, religions, perspectives on life, and that's something quite special.

So I think it's a privilege to be a student athlete, because not everybody can tell about themselves that they go to university study and also do their sport and also just, you know, making friends.

I think it's so much fun. I always try to finish everything as soon as possible.

So then I'm I'm free to enjoy my day with my friends or doing new experiences, I feel like, what makes it better as an athlete here is really the trainer, like, obviously for me, having, like, my meniscus torn and being through all the injuries and having to play on it, she's really keeping me going right now, just because I'm training with her consistently, where our coaches definitely set the standard from day one, whether it's from the recruitment process to practice the weights, you know, they make sure we're always on point and, you know, ready for anything.

Not a lot of people get to train every day.

Have all the resources.

Have a coach, have a PT, have people to push you.

I understand that it's an absolute privilege to wear the eagle on a Saturday, and it's something that many people don't get the opportunity to do.

Visit

Nestled in the heart of Pulaski, TN, the University of Tennessee Southern is dedicated to putting students first, catering to the diverse needs of our small-town community.

As a destination campus deeply committed to the student experience, we prioritize both academic excellence and the personal growth of every student.

UT Southern proudly stands as the fourth undergraduate campus in the UT System, serving as the sole public four-year institution of higher education between Chattanooga and Memphis.

Conveniently located along Tennessee’s southern border, our campus is situated approximately 70 miles south of Nashville and 40 miles north of Huntsville, Alabama.

Here's what makes us stand out: We offer 38 areas of study across six schools, providing tailored learning experiences with small classes and esteemed professors.

Our academic divisions focus on business, education, humanities, mathematics and sciences, nursing, and social sciences.

With a robust athletics department boasting 19 teams across 11 sports, UT Southern has something for everyone. We prioritize character development through 19 NAIA varsity sports, with an impressive record of 40 Mid-South Conference Championships and 12 National Championships.

Our commitment to success extends beyond the field, with 75 Athletic All-Americans and 215 Academic All-Americans recognized. Offering 11 Men's, 12 Women's, and 2 Coed Sports, we provide a comprehensive athletic experience.

UT Southern is dedicated to evolving our curriculum to reflect industry trends and technological advancements, emphasizing interdisciplinary studies for a well-rounded education.

We empower students to discover their passions, foster critical thinking skills, and graduate prepared for successful careers in an ever-changing world. At UT Southern, excellence is not just a goal—it's our commitment to every student who walks through our doors.

transcripts.transcript:

Here you'll spark your passion under the guidance of our nation's brightest minds who open a window to the world's wonders from close to home, you'll fan the fires of competition on the field, the court or the course honing skills you never knew you had to accomplish what you never thought you could.

You'll do it all while forging bonds that will last a lifetime and serving a community that values your talents, because here we think the best way to find yourself is to look beyond yourself.

There's a future waiting for you.

We'll help you build it.

Because what defines greatness as a single choice to not condemn the darkness, but to light a fire.

pins.name: Corban University
pins.description:
Cascade Collegiate Conference

Visit

Corban University Athletics is committed to fielding teams of Christian student athletes who represent Christ and the University at a top level of competition. Athletics at Corban exists to integrate and enhance the mission of the University, while providing student-athletes and the college community opportunities for spiritual, academic, and athletic growth and development.

We understand, from the Christian perspective, that competition is healthy for growing maturing Christians student-athletes. Studentathletes who are fortunate enough to be a Warrior are provided and challenged with enriched, quality, and competitive intercollegiate athletic opportunities at a national level.

Personal growth is highly emphasized and enhanced by combining spiritual truth into athletic and academic achievement. Coaches actively recruit student-athletes who are committed to developing Christlike character through discipline, teamwork, competition, and ministry. It is a primary goal that all our young men and women display that character and attitude toward opponents, spectators, officials and the community.

Student-athletes at Corban can expect to be challenged, instructed, encouraged and mentored in the process of growing and living life in the image of Jesus Christ. As a member of the Cascade Collegiate Conference (CCC), Corban is affiliated with the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA). Warrior teams compete in women's basketball, cross country, track & field, golf, soccer, softball, lacrosse, volleyball and beach volleyball along with the men's sports of basketball, baseball, cross country, track & field, golf, wrestling and soccer.

Corban has claimed 43 CCC Championships (23 regular-season championships; 20 tournament championships) since all Warrior sports joined the CCC in 1994. Since joining the NAIA prior to the 1970-71 year, Corban University has competed in 44 regional tournament and 83 national tournaments.

In 2022, the Corban beach volleyball team claimed the inaugural NAIA Beach Volleyball National Invitational, Robert Swoboda won the individual national title in the NAIA Track & Field 10,000-meter race, and Valerie Schmidt was crowned the NAIA National Champion in the heptathlon.

The 2022-23 school year featured a pair of NAIA National Tournament Runner-Up team titles for the women's volleyball and beach volleyball programs, where the NAIA National Attacker of the Year (Rylee Troutman) and NAIA Most Valuable Player (Avari Ridgway) paved the way for the two powerhouse rosters.

On an individual basis, Corban men's wrestling standout student-athlete David Rubio set the new standard for the young program, securing his second consecutive CCC Championship at the 165-weight class and finishing as the National Runner-Up at the NAIA National Tournament, the highest individual finish in program history.

At EOU, students can pursue a wide range of academic disciplines, guided by dedicated faculty who prioritize hands-on learning and individualized attention.

The university's emphasis on experiential education equips students with practical skills and knowledge to excel in their chosen fields.

In addition to its academic excellence, EOU boasts a robust athletic program that competes in the Cascade Collegiate Conference and in the Frontier Conference (Football) of the NAIA.

Whether students are pursuing academic endeavors or athletic ambitions, Eastern Oregon University offers a supportive and enriching community where individuals can realize their full potential and create lasting memories.

transcripts.transcript:
I would say the feel of grace is definitely like being at home.

It's so beautiful, and there's tons of green space and the lake, and you just have all this nature around us.

It wasn't just about learning the content.

It wasn't just about a specific degree.

Was about who I was as a person.

It was about who I was as a believer.

It was about who I am as an employee and as a part of the community.

I feel like most of the professors on campus give, give and give and give and give because they believe that their students are here for a reason, for a purpose, that their calling is so much bigger than just a job.

There's just something about being here at school where you'll just walk in and everyone's like, so welcoming to you.

It's just such a different environment than I'm used to.

You walk outside and 50 students are just spread out throughout the campus on the lawns, just doing homework, playing games, whether it's like spike ball or Frisbee.

There's just so many places for students just to go and hang out.

Having this small campus with all these beautiful places and open areas just makes it really easy to feel like you're kind of home, or that feel like you're part of the community right away.

Well, I really like to know my students.

I like to get to know them.

I like to get to understand them, how they're how they're wired.

How can I connect with them in the classroom so that I can foster their learning, so that they can become the professional they need to be.

They learn all this stuff.

They have these aha moments.

They run out, they come back, the next day, you'll have no idea what I did.

I was watching somebody, and then I helped them, and it was so rewarding.

And I'm like, Yes, that's what you're supposed to do.

It empowers them.

I want them to be what they want to be.

And I'm like, How do I get them to do that?

That's like, my greatest challenge as a professor.

Really didn't have plans for college, and at the advice of my father, he said, Well, you know what, just apply for one school.

So my education at Grace, both in the undergraduate and the MBA, have set the stage for me to continue to develop myself and my my knowledge regarding this field.

One of the things that always impressed me about Grace College was they weren't just located in Winona lake.

They were really integrated into those communities.

They were a part of what was happening there.

They were reaching out to some of the organizations and some of the just the neighborhoods that they existed in.

There are a lot of quality people here trying to better our world, that mentality is what we're pushing on to our students, like a lot of classes, faith is just integrated into it.

They want to talk about everything from at least a faith aspect.

That foundation that I set at Grace has has helped me to be a better father, has helped me to be a better employee, has helped me to be a better husband.

That's probably almost more valuable than the education, and that's something that I don't think you probably would get at every college.

transcripts.transcript:
Hello and welcome to this video tour of Bellevue University's main campus.

We're happy to have you with us to show you our beautiful, 46 acre campus in Bellevue Nebraska.

We'll start our journey at the Marge H Durham Student Center, built in 1986 the Student Center serves as a student hub for dining services.

Has patio space for bonfires and hanging out, recreation space for campus events and even a game room.

Less than a block from main campus is the new student housing Betts road complex, open in the fall of 2017 The complex has 18 units with 72 single rooms.

Each apartment has four single bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen, a living area and furnishings, including a washer and dryer in each unit.

Next up is the Gordon loggier Athletic Center.

The Athletic Center houses the Jerry mosser court administrative offices and the new eSports arena deemed the Bruin bunker.

The facility is home to the university's NAIA sanctioned sports programs, baseball, softball, volleyball, men's and women's basketball, men's and women's golf, men's and women's soccer and men's and women's cross country.

The CO Ed esports team competes in League of Legends Overwatch and Hearthstone.

What would a college campus be without a library?

The Freeman logger library has the largest library collection in Sarpy County, along with plenty of books, the library includes an integrated media center, which allows students access to computerized and web based resources with training facilities to teach students how to effectively use these resources.

Located in the back hall of the library, the Learning Commons is an important support office with consultants and peer tutors ready to assist you in the tutor and study skills program and writing center.

North of the Learning Center is the newest building on campus, built in 2021 the sustainability lab is complete with a greenhouse, algae pond and more.

Our next stop is the Educational Services Building.

The Educational Services Building, ESB, as is known, houses, classrooms and the College of Science and Technology on its lower level.

On the middle and upper levels, there are additional College of Arts and Science faculty and staff offices, Career Services is also found on the third floor.

Everyone's favorite thing about this building seems to be the amazing indoor waterfall.

Attached to the ESB is the John B Muller Administrative Services Building, or ASB, built in 2011 the ASB is the tallest building in Bellevue Nebraska.

Right inside the front doors is the One Stop Welcome Center and support desk.

One Stop provides a one stop shop for current and prospective students to meet with admissions advising and financial services, staff disability services, as well as scholarships and grants.

Are other helpful resources located in the ASB the Bruin training and athletic center is a regular stop for Bruin student athletes, and has wellness equipment and a weight room that are free for all students to use.

We hope you enjoyed this tour of Bell University's main campus.

See you soon.

Recognized as one of the top public regional colleges in the Midwest and one of America’s “Best Colleges” for 26 consecutive years by U.S. News, VCSU is an academically driven, student-centered university.

VCSU offers more than 65 undergraduate programs in art, business, communication arts, computer systems and software engineering, education, kinesiology and human performance, language and literature, mathematics, music, science, social science, and technology education.

Founded in 1890 as a teacher’s college, VCSU has held fast to its heritage and maintains an outstanding reputation for developing some of the finest K – 12 educators in the region.

By providing full-time students with their own laptop, VCSU has remained committed to accessible, technology-driven educational opportunities for all students.

Adapting educational technology and teaching methods has ensured all students receive a high-impact learning experience no matter their location or ability.

transcripts.transcript:
What defines you? If you want better results, you must ask better questions.

The right questions awaken incredible power, opening the mind to possibilities and banishing the word impossible.

La Sierra University is defined by the questions it asks.

How can we seek truth and enlarge human understanding through scholarship?

How can we know God ourselves and the world?

How can we serve others and contribute to the good of our local and global communities?

La Sierra University relentlessly asked these fundamental, yet all encompassing questions, the answers have led us to excellence.

We started in a field in 1922 the dust blew so thick that students shoveled it from their dorm rooms, but the founders clung to their vision of values based higher education.

Now la Sierra is a thriving campus of Riverside the city of arts and innovation. We offer more than degrees.

We teach students to be fully alive, to take radical ownership of their faith, their career, their community, their country and their world.

Students dig in one of the longest running excavations in Jordan and study abroad and serve as missionaries in dozens of countries.

They perform in prestigious competitions and venues around the world.

They represent the United States on world stages as the undergraduates.

They co author research in leading publications.

They are athletes who learn that teamwork, discipline and perseverance are the keys to success in all of life's endeavors.

All this defines who we are at La Sierra University, I ask again, what defines you?

The Nevada State athletics teams are called the Scorpions.

Nevada State University opened in 2002 as the only four-year, teaching-focused institution in the Nevada System of Higher Education, situated between the state’s research universities and community colleges. The university launched athletics in July 2025 with Women’s Flag Football and Men’s Track & Field, competing as an independent institution for the first season. The university joined the NAIA and the GSAC in July 2026, coinciding with the addition of Women’s and Men’s Cross Country and Women’s Track & Field. The athletics department plans to add additional sports in the coming years with a commitment to building steadily, responsibly, and with long-term success in mind.

transcripts.transcript:
College athletics.

It is the proving ground for elite high school athletes who wish to measure their skill, willpower and fortitude against others who also excel in their craft.

It is not an arena made for the undisciplined or unmotivated.

It rewards those who push their bodies to the limit and punishes the excuse makers for the focused competitors.

The choice of institution will play a pivotal role in how they transition from the glories of high school to the potential of what they can achieve.

St Ambrose is a university where student athletes, serious about academics and being the best they can be in competition, can thrive to their absolute potential.

What distinguishes athletics at St Ambrose as members of our athletic family fighting bee athletes play and practice in facilities which are among the finest to be found in the NAIA.

The Ambrose dome is an indoor facility with batting cages and a golf simulator where outdoor sports can train in winter months and in foul weather.

The Wellness and Recreation Center has a weight room dedicated to athletic teams, as well as an additional weight room and cardio room for all students.

It features a dance studio where competitive dance and cheer can practice routines.

The field house features an indoor track facility with long jump, pole vault, high jump and throwing cages, two wood courts and two courts with multi use surface allow practice space for every sport, including tennis.

Lee Lowman arena hosts basketball, wrestling, volleyball and Winter Guard.

And last year, was the site of the NAIA national cheer and dance competition. Modern Woodman Park is not only home to the Kansas City Royals minor league team, Quad City river bandits, but also hosts the fighting bee baseball program.

St Vincent Sports Complex has a dedicated softball field, as well as three turfed fields that host lacrosse and soccer games, and has practice facilities for football and marching band.

Brady Street stadium is the site for st Ambrose football, providing a vibrant Game Day atmosphere, which includes tailgating, marching band dance performances and cheerleading.

Members of fighting bee Athletics will not only enjoy the finest facilities, but will also discover the st Ambrose difference as they cultivate relationships during their experiences, student athletes at sau develop deep bonds with athletic staff at every level, from assistant coaches, head coaches, five athletic trainers, sports information staff, all the way to the athletic director st Ambrose cares about our athletes having a great experience.

It is when top facilities combine with a relationship driven staff that the student athlete at St Ambrose unlocks their potential, finds the best of what they can become, and experiences the transition from what could be to the summit of achievement.

Cumberland University Athletic Department
Statement of Mission, Philosophy and Objective

Mission

The purpose of the intercollegiate athletic program at Cumberland University is to instill in every student-athlete the highest standards of personal integrity and responsibility.

Philosophy

The Cumberland University intercollegiate athletic program provides the opportunity for each student-athlete to develop self-discipline through the setting and achievement of goals in the classroom and in their respective sport.

Objectives

The Cumberland University intercollegiate athletic program is dedicated to:

  • Providing equal opportunity for intercollegiate participation for male and female student-athletes, and all minorities.
  • Supporting the satisfactory academic progress of each student-athlete.

Hey guys, I'm Josh, and we're in the Hutcherson center, and this is where our women's volleyball team plays, and our men's and women's basketball team, if you look around, you can tell it's a brand new court and a very nice facility.

You'll see our national championship banners, all the red banners that you see, all of those belong to men's or women's, indoor or outdoor track and field, except for one, and that belongs to men's soccer.

Our men's soccer team went down to Florida in 2017 ranked 23rd in the nation.

Had to have a play in game to get into the championship and won the semifinal and quarterfinal games on penalty kicks, and finally, the championship game on a golden goal opportunity.

So a fantastic story, but our track and field program is our most successful program as far as national championships go, every single year between the really four distinctive sports, men and women's, indoor and outdoor track and field, they have an opportunity to win a national championship.

Behind me, you can see some of our flying Queens banners.

That's our women's basketball team, the AAU championship banners that they have.

We're actually going to go into their locker room and talk a little more about their history.

All right, guys.

Now we're in the flying Queens locker room, which is one of our premier locker rooms that we have here at Wayland Baptist University.

This one, for sure, did not come without a lot of hard work and history. Our women's basketball program is the winningest collegiate basketball program in all of the United States.

We're talking UConn women, Tennessee women, UCLA men, Duke men, anybody you can think of, Wayland, Babbage University.

Flying Queens has more wins than any of them. And that flying Queens name, I know, might sound a little strange to you, but it has a really neat story behind it.

The girls were beating everybody in this area, and so a local aviator, Mr. Hutcherson, said, Hey, let's take these girls and try to find some competitions.

They started flying all over the country playing basketball games and in the early 50s and 60s and stuff, they were they had the longest win streak in collegiate basketball history as well, 131 games in a row.

That record still stands today. So the program itself was nominated for the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame several times, and before they got in, they were losing to the names of like Shaquille, O'Neal, Allen, Iverson, Tom Izzo, Yao Ming, Tracy, McGrady, Cheryl swoops, just to give you an idea, we're talking about the greatest names in basketball history.

But in 2019 our girls were finally enshrined into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, which is something we're very proud of, and has a ton of awesome, rich history included.

So now let's go check out another piece of the hutch. Alright guys, we're here in the entryway of the Hutchison center, and what you'll see up here is end to end, wall to wall, trophy cases, and this has things like individual awards, like all American status and team awards, national championships and things like that.

But the one thing that I really want to point out is a an overall Wayland competition, and something that we're really proud of is the Learfield Sports directors cup.

Thanks.
